content: Managing pesticides in agriculture and public health is a critical area of focus for both the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Health Organization (WHO). The second edition of the compendium, published in 2021, provides a comprehensive collection of FAO and WHO guidelines, toolkits, and other resources aimed at supporting the International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management. These resources are designed to guide the management of pesticides throughout their entire life cycle, from production to disposal, and are particularly targeted at governments in lowand middle-income countries, though they may also be useful to other stakeholders. The compendium emphasizes that the designations and presentation of materials within the document do not reflect any legal or developmental status of countries, territories, or regions, nor do they imply endorsement of specific companies or products. The views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily represent the policies of FAO or WHO. The publication is available under a Creative Commons license, allowing for non-commercial use, adaptation, and redistribution, provided proper citation is given. Translations must include a disclaimer stating that FAO and WHO are not responsible for the content or accuracy of the translation. The guidelines cover a wide range of topics, including pesticide legislation, policy development, registration, compliance, enforcement, and post-registration surveillance. They also address the management of highly hazardous pesticides (HHPs), public health pesticides, and household pesticides. The resources are regularly updated to ensure their relevance and validity. Key Guidelines and Resources: 1. Guidance on Pesticide Legislation: This document provides detailed instructions for governments on drafting or revising national pesticide laws. It outlines the typical contents of pesticide legislation, the drafting process, and the importance of linking laws to national pesticide policies and regulatory programs. It also highlights the need for institutional structures to coordinate pesticide management across different stages of the pesticide life cycle. 2. Guidance on Pest and Pesticide Management Policy Development: This guidance advises governments on creating policies that reduce pesticide risks and promote sustainable agricultural production. It emphasizes integrated pest management (IPM), including biological control, as a sustainable approach to pest management. The document also links pesticide management to environmental protection, human health, food safety, and trade. 3. Guidelines on Highly Hazardous Pesticides (HHPs): These guidelines outline a three-step process to identify, assess, and mitigate the risks associated with HHPs. They provide a definition of HHPs based on the International Code of Conduct and criteria developed by the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Management (JMPM). The guidelines also discuss international conventions and frameworks addressing HHPs, such as the Stockholm and Rotterdam Conventions. 4. Guidance on Management of Household Pesticides: This document focuses on strengthening the regulation and oversight of household pesticides and educating the public on effective pest and pesticide management in domestic settings. It is primarily intended for government authorities but may also be useful to the pesticide industry and non-governmental organizations. 5. FAOLEX Database: This is one of the world’s largest electronic collections of national laws and regulations on food, agriculture, and renewable natural resources. It includes pesticide laws, regulations, and policies from various countries. 6. Guidance on Policy-Making for Integrated Vector Management (IVM): This guidance supports managers of vector control programs in developing policies for IVM, which promotes interdisciplinary collaboration and the judicious use of pesticides. It emphasizes risk prevention, safe disposal of pesticide waste, and the involvement of multiple sectors and stakeholders. 7. Guidelines on Public Health Pesticide Management Policy: Separate guidelines are available for the WHO South-East Asia Region and the WHO African Region. These documents guide national policymakers in developing, implementing, and evaluating policies for managing public health pesticides, including those used for vector control and household purposes. The compendium also includes resources on pesticide registration, quality control, advertising, distribution, and disposal. It provides tools for risk assessment, efficacy evaluation, and the prevention of pesticide resistance. Additionally, it offers guidance on public education and training for pesticide application and management. The FAO and WHO emphasize the importance of reducing reliance on pesticides, selecting low-risk products, and ensuring their proper use. These principles are central to the tiered approach to pesticide risk reduction outlined in the guidelines. The compendium serves as a vital resource for governments and other stakeholders working to improve pesticide management and reduce associated risks to human health and the environment.
